analysis.title: Duttenhoefer's Daily 07.10.2026
key_insights: S&P 500 rose 58bps to 7818 (+14% YTD), a new all-time high (#28 in 2026) despite macro worries. Momentum and small caps are clear laggards. GS Power Up America basket (GSENEPOW) leads at +4.5%.
Cross-asset levels cited: US 10yr 5.31%, Brent $102, Gold $4136, Bitcoin $84k. FOMC minutes are due today and earnings season starts next week.
Google and Constellation Energy announced a deal under which Constellation invests $4.3bn to upgrade 11 nuclear units, adding 890 MW of new capacity from 2028-32.
ISM services prices-paid index rose to 74 in September, the highest since July 2022. Tariffs and fuel costs were the most cited pressures, and no industry reported lower prices paid.

Microsoft cut its projected internal spending on Claude by more than one third (expected to spend over $1bn), and Meta's internal users of the Claude Code assistant fell from roughly 60k to 30k. Both firms encourage staff to use internal options.
SpaceX is seeking to raise $40bn in a financing led by Apollo to buy Nvidia chips: $10bn in bank loans and $30bn in investment-grade debt.
Apple plans a push into smart home devices (doorbell, thermostat and other accessories, in partnership with LG Electronics). New Apple devices are set to be introduced on 13 Oct.
Marvell's capital markets day was well received. Management outlined FY31 targets including a 55%-60% revenue CAGR over FY26-31 at 56-59% gross margin. GS raised its estimates by 13% on average.

Trading desk color (Peter Bartlett): the NDX breakout is driven by clean positioning (GS PB hedge fund nets near a 5-year low, GS Sentiment indicator near multi-year lows), covering of macro hedges, and concentration into Tech/AI while market breadth is at its lowest since 2000.

US semis preview: GS sees upside to estimates across most sub-sectors. After a pullback over the past 2 months (SOX -11% vs SPX +4%), the trading setup into earnings is more constructive than the cautious 2Q setup.

Q3 earnings preview: consensus expects S&P 500 EPS growth of 27% y/y. AI infrastructure spending accounts for over 50% of S&P 500 EPS growth, alongside hyperscaler capex growth of 116%. Median S&P stock EPS growth is about 9% (vs 14% in Q2).
GS economists estimate higher rates will subtract only about 0.2% from 2027 GDP growth, based on the effects on housing, consumption and capex.
Nvidia's market cap above $5700bn exceeds the combined market cap of the smallest 251 S&P 500 companies.
Agent access: Amazon recently blocked Meta's Muse AI agent from its retail site, and the note expects websites to protect their traffic from AI agents.
